claim.pdf_says: Figure D.3 — Compilation group and run unit structures is a nested-box schematic: a heavy-bordered COMPILATION GROUP box at the top containing three sub-boxes (a left compilation-unit column with an arrow labelled "To other run unit", a centre compilation-unit box, and a right compilation-unit column with an arrow labelled "To other run unit"); inside the centre box a source-unit box holds the dashed source element "P-1", beneath which sit the source units "P-1-1" and "P-1-2", and inside "P-1-2" the two dashed source elements "P-1-2-1" and "P-1-2-2". Arrows lead down to a second heavy-bordered RUN UNIT box at the bottom, whose interior repeats the same nesting in runtime-module / runtime-element form, with inbound arrows labelled "From other comp. group".

claim.why_it_matters: Every piece of information the figure carries lives in its box nesting and arrows, not in its labels. The markdown keeps only the floating labels, so the reader cannot recover which entities are compilation units versus source units versus source elements, that P-1-2-1 and P-1-2-2 are nested inside P-1-2, that P-1 is a source element of the centre compilation unit, or that the compilation group maps onto the run unit at all. The entire lower (run unit) half of the figure has no representation whatsoever. Read literally, the transcription looks like a stray list of program names.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED at the 300 dpi render of PDF page 1074 (printed page 1044), with two corrections to how the claim was stated.

What the PDF actually shows (verified against the full page plus four zoomed crops):
  * Intro paragraph + caption 'Figure D.3 — Compilation group and run unit structures' — both transcribed correctly in the markdown.
  * UPPER schematic: one heavy-bordered box (= Compilation Group) enclosing three solid-bordered boxes (= Compilation Units): a tall empty left column, a centre box, and a tall empty right column. Inside the centre compilation unit is a thin-bordered Source Unit box; inside that, a wide dashed Source Element labelled 'P-1'; beneath it two thin-bordered Source Units labelled 'P-1-1' and 'P-1-2'. P-1-1 contains one dashed Source Element. P-1-2 contains its own dashed Source Element plus two further thin-bordered Source Units labelled 'P-1-2-1' and 'P-1-2-2', each containing a dashed Source Element.
  * ARROWS: a down-arrow leaves the left compilation unit labelled 'To other run unit'; the same on the right; a bracket spanning the compilation group feeds a down-arrow into the Run Unit box; two down-arrows enter the run unit's left and right runtime-module columns labelled 'From other comp. group'.
  * LOWER schematic: a second heavy-bordered box (= Run Unit) whose interior repeats the identical nesting in Runtime Module / Runtime Element form. Critically, EVERY box in the lower half is UNLABELLED — the lower schematic contains no text at all.
  * LEGEND (right margin, two stacks): heavy border = Compilation Group; medium solid = Compilation Unit; thin solid = Source Unit; dashed = Source Element. Then heavy border = Run Unit; THIN SOLID = Runtime Module; dashed = Runtime Element.

The discrepancy is genuine and is not formatting, reflow, hyphenation or page-break furniture. Figure D.3 is a purely topological diagram: its entire semantic payload is containment and arrow direction, and the markdown carries zero topology. Nothing in lines 10-18 tells a reader that P-1-2-1 and P-1-2-2 are nested inside P-1-2, that P-1 is a source element of the centre compilation unit, that there are three compilation units of which two are empty, or that the compilation group maps onto a run unit. Read literally the transcription is a stray list of program names followed by four orphan arrow labels. The prose above the figure explicitly relies on the picture ('shows schematically, in an example, the relationships between the components of a compilation group and their corresponding runtime entities'), so the lost structure is exactly the content the paragraph defers to.

CORRECTION 1 to the claim's quotation — the claim truncated the markdown. Lines 20-33 of page-1074.md DO carry a '**Legend**' heading plus two tables listing Compilation Group / Compilation Unit / Source Unit / Source Element and Run Unit / Runtime Module / Runtime Element. So the vocabulary of entity kinds survives, and the claim's 'the entire lower (run unit) half of the figure has no representation whatsoever' is overstated: the lower half's legend and its two 'From other comp. group' arrow labels are transcribed. What is unrecoverable is not the vocabulary but the ASSIGNMENT — the markdown never associates any legend term with any label or with any other label, so the legend rows describe border styles for boxes that do not exist anywhere in the document and are therefore vacuous as transcribed. Note also that a text-only transcription could not have carried labels out of the lower schematic in any case, because the PDF draws it entirely unlabelled; the loss there is the nesting, not missing text.

CORRECTION 2 — the claim understates the defect, because the legend the transcriber added is itself WRONG. The 'Symbol' column is transcriber interpolation (the PDF's legend column contains drawn boxes, not words), and row 'Runtime Module' is described as '(dashed border box)' when the PDF unambiguously draws it as a solid thin-bordered box, identical in style to Source Unit / Compilation Unit — see the zoomed crop of the lower legend. As transcribed, Runtime Module and Runtime Element are both 'dashed', which collapses the module/element distinction that this figure exists to draw. 'Runtime Element' is likewise called '(small dashed border box)' when the PDF box is a plain dashed rectangle the same size and style as Source Element, and 'Compilation Group' / 'Run Unit' are called '(solid double border box)' when the PDF draws a single heavy rule, not a double rule. This is an affirmative factual error layered on top of the structural loss, not merely an omission.

Severity 'structural' and kind 'missing-figure' are both correct classifications. Annex D is informative, so no normative rule is lost, but the figure is the definitional illustration of compilation group / compilation unit / source unit / source element versus run unit / runtime module / runtime element — terminology COBOL.NET uses throughout — and it is not reconstructible from the transcription.
verdict.corrected_description: Figure D.3 (page 1074 = printed 1044) is a two-tier nested-box schematic whose entire information content is containment and arrow topology. The markdown transcription reduces it to five floating labels (P-1, P-1-1, P-1-2, P-1-2-1, P-1-2-2), four orphan arrow captions, and a transcriber-written Legend table — with no boxes, no nesting, and no arrows. Consequently the reader cannot recover: (a) that the outer heavy box is the Compilation Group and it holds THREE Compilation Units, of which the left and right are drawn empty; (b) that P-1 is a Source Element inside a Source Unit inside the centre Compilation Unit; (c) that P-1-1 and P-1-2 are Source Units beneath it and that P-1-2-1 and P-1-2-2 are Source Units nested INSIDE P-1-2, each holding a dashed Source Element; (d) that a heavy-bordered Run Unit box below repeats the identical nesting in Runtime Module / Runtime Element form (all of whose boxes are unlabelled in the PDF, so no text was available to carry across); or (e) the arrow topology — 'To other run unit' leaving the outer compilation units, the compilation group feeding down into the run unit, and 'From other comp. group' entering the outer runtime modules. Beyond this structural loss, the markdown Legend contains an affirmative error introduced by the transcriber: 'Runtime Module' is described as '(dashed border box)' when the PDF draws a solid thin-bordered box, which makes Runtime Module and Runtime Element indistinguishable in the transcription; 'Runtime Element' is called '(small dashed border box)' when it is a plain dashed box identical to Source Element; and the heavy single rules on 'Compilation Group' and 'Run Unit' are called '(solid double border box)'. The claim's own quotation of the markdown was truncated — it omitted the Legend block — so its assertion that the run-unit half has 'no representation whatsoever' is too strong: the lower legend and the two 'From other comp. group' captions are present. The correct statement is that the figure's box nesting and arrow topology are absent in both halves, and that the surviving legend is unanchored to any label and partly wrong.
